Abstract Factory: You only need to create one product type
The "families" only have one member each
Adapter: You control both interfaces — just align them directly
The codebase already has an adapter for this backend
Bridge: You only have one dimension of variation
Adapter already solves your interop problem
Builder: Constructor takes ≤4 args and they are all required
Object has no optional or step-wise configuration
A simple object literal { a, b, c } would do the job
Chain of Responsibility: All handlers always run regardless of result
The chain is fixed at compile time and never reordered
Command: You're calling a single method directly with no need for queueing/undo/logging
The action has no state and never needs to be reified
You'd be wrapping every UI event in a command class
Composite: The hierarchy is one or two levels deep
Leaves and composites have nothing meaningful in common
A simple recursive function over a plain object tree would suffice
Decorator: Behavior is fixed and known at compile time
Higher-order functions or middleware patterns already solve it (e.g. Redux/Zustand middleware)
Only one wrapper layer is needed
Facade: The subsystem already has a simple public API
The facade would just re-export everything
You'd be creating a facade with one method that calls one underlying method
Factory Method: You only have one concrete product type and no realistic plan for a second
The "factory" would be a one-liner that returns new Foo() with no logic
The codebase already has a factory for this domain
Iterator: A native for...of over an array or Map already works
The collection is a simple array
You'd need an entire iterator class for one consumer
Mediator: Two components only talk to each other
You'd be introducing a mediator with one method that calls one component
Observer or event bus already does what you need
Memento: You can serialize state to JSON and back
You only need one undo step
Observer: A single store subscription would do
Only one consumer needs the event
Prototype: A plain structuredClone() or spread operator does the job
The object has a constructor you can call
Proxy: You can use JavaScript's built-in Proxy global
A simple lazy getter (get foo() { return this.foo ??= compute() }) suffices
The "proxy" doesn't add behavior beyond delegation
Singleton: A store slice or DI container would do
The "singleton" is just stateless utility functions
You only need it for convenient access from anywhere
State: States never share a common interface meaningfully
A useState hook or store flag does the job
Strategy: You only have one algorithm and no plan for a second
A simple switch over 2-3 cases is clearer than 3 strategy classes
Template Method: You only have one concrete subclass
Visitor: The hierarchy has only 2-3 element classes
You'd be adding a Visitor for a single operation
A discriminated union with switch over kind field is clearer
